pathway.title: Snap Inc — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Liquidity is the anchor of the credit and is large against what falls due, but it is being spent. Cash and cash equivalents of USD 1,019,215 thousand plus marketable securities of USD 1,751,432 thousand give liquid assets of USD 2,770,647 thousand, which is 4.47x the USD 620,509 thousand of notes due by 2028 and 0.81x all principal of USD 3,420,509 thousand, before an undrawn USD 1.05 billion revolving facility. Liquid assets nonetheless fell by USD 605,632 thousand, or 17.94%, from the end of 2024, a period in which buybacks exceeded free cash flow by USD 590,658 thousand, and the cushion will keep shrinking if buybacks continue to run above free cash flow. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 155–156; calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C08

Earnings quality is the main constraint: EBITDA before add-backs is close to zero and the issuer's adjusted measure leaves out a recurring cost that Snap pays for in cash through buybacks. For the last twelve months to 30 September 2026, EBITDA before add-backs was USD 59,536 thousand, 0.91% of revenue, against issuer-adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,223,341 thousand, and stock-based compensation of USD 1,025,256 thousand is most of the gap. In nine months 2026 the shares Snap repurchased equalled 100.62% of the shares that vested from stock awards, so buybacks of USD 600,964 thousand did little more than hold the Class A share count, which rose 0.41%. Free cash flow of USD 776,554 thousand therefore overstates what is left for creditors, and counting stock pay as a cash cost would make it negative USD 248,702 thousand, an analyst normalisation. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 144; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 56; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C05; calculation C09

Leverage is moderate on the issuer's measure and unreadable on the unadjusted one, so debt service has to be judged on cash. Total debt at carrying value of USD 3,486,418 thousand at 30 September 2026 is 2.85x last twelve months issuer-adjusted EBITDA but 58.56x last twelve months EBITDA before add-backs, and cash interest paid of USD 151.06 million over the same period is covered 8.10x and 0.39x respectively. Free cash flow covers the USD 145.3 million of interest due within a year 5.34x, so debt service is comfortable on cash, but the interest bill is stepping up as the 2025 refinancing replaced near-zero-coupon convertible notes with senior notes, with contractual interest on the notes up 46.00% in nine months 2026. Net of both cash lines, debt is USD 715,771 thousand. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 155; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C07

Maturities are well spaced, and the refinancing test comes in 2028, not 2027. Only USD 106,318 thousand of convertible notes due on 1 May 2027 and an undrawn USD 250.0 million facility tranche expiring on 6 May 2027 fall due before 2028, and the USD 514,191 thousand of convertible notes due in March 2028 is the first large maturity. The convertible notes cannot be counted on to convert: the April 2026 average buyback price of USD 5.15 was 23.22% of the 2030 notes' conversion price of USD 22.18 and the if-converted value stayed below principal, so they behave as cash debt. The 2033 and 2034 senior notes were quoted at 94.56% and 93.85% of principal at 30 September 2026, about 9 points lower than at the end of 2025, so market access exists but is priced; replacing the 2028 and 2030 convertible notes at the senior notes' rate would add USD 82.52 million a year of interest, 10.63% of last twelve months free cash flow, on the analyst's assumption. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 19–24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-03-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 156; 10-Q_2026-06-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 160; calculation C08; calculation C13; calculation C16

Revenue durability is average at best: revenue is growing, but advertising is short-cycle, concentrated and slowing. Advertising is 80.38% of nine-month 2026 revenue and grew 5.33% against 15.07% for total revenue; most advertisers have no long-term commitments, and Snap states that demand growth on its advertising platform has slowed and that platform policy changes have hurt targeting and measurement, particularly in North America, where the growth in daily users was negative 6% in the third quarter of 2026. Other revenue, up 85.31%, includes a fixed-fee partner contract with USD 387.9 million unsatisfied at the end of 2025 that is disclosed only through the first quarter of 2027, and the part that is subscriptions is not reported. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 38–41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 172; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11

Margin resilience is improving because costs are almost flat, which is real but partly one-off. In nine months 2026 revenue rose 15.07% while total costs rose 4.62%, an incremental operating margin of 65.08%, and in the third quarter revenue rose 14.31% against a 0.65% rise in costs, turning an operating loss of USD 128,362 thousand into an operating profit of USD 76,716 thousand. Gross margin rose to 59.13% from 53.33% as content and developer partner costs fell, and the 16% headcount reduction cost USD 128,505 thousand, inside the issuer's estimate of USD 95 million to USD 130 million. The savings rely on cuts that cannot repeat, hosting and other commitments of USD 1,609,584 thousand in 2026 and USD 1,075,237 thousand in 2027 floor the cost base, and the same operating leverage works in reverse if revenue stalls. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 44–46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; 10-Q_2026-03-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 186; calculation C10; calculation C12; calculation C14

Cash conversion is a genuine strength, but the cash goes to equity holders first. Purchases of property and equipment are only 2.94% of revenue because hosting is rented, so last twelve months free cash flow is 63.48% of issuer-adjusted EBITDA and 11.83% of revenue, and nine-month 2026 free cash flow of USD 570,998 thousand is more than double the USD 231,633 thousand of a year earlier. Buybacks took USD 600,964 thousand of it and more, and fourth-quarter seasonality adds support, since fourth-quarter 2025 revenue was 13.91% above the third quarter. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 143; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 155; calculation C04; calculation C06; calculation C15

Platform-harm litigation and regulation are the primary downside path and cannot be sized. Thousands of plaintiffs allege that the platform harms minors, attorney general trials are set for August 2027, the European Commission opened proceedings under the Digital Services Act on 26 March 2026, and insurers contest coverage, with a hearing on 10 December 2026. Snap states that no loss can be estimated, settlements so far were not material and a USD 65.0 million securities settlement was covered by insurance, but the filing cites a competitor settlement of over USD 12 billion, a reminder that these claims sit outside debt and outside the figures above. Liquid assets are large against anything disclosed, so the effect would arrive first as lost cushion rather than as a payment default. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 27–30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 131–132; 10-Q_2026-06-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 25; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C07

Financial policy is the swing factor: founder control, thin note-level limits and a buyback habit mean creditors rely on restraint. The Business & governance review found two founders with over 99% of the votes, indentures that do not restrict debt, liens or payouts, and a revolving facility whose USD 800.0 million minimum-liquidity covenant tests cash and cash equivalents, which were USD 1,019,215 thousand at 30 September 2026; headroom is not computed because the covenant is known only from a summary. Nothing documented is creditor-adverse, but nothing in the notes prevents it. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 156

runs.text: The five main strengths rank as follows. First, liquid assets of USD 2,770,647 thousand cover the USD 620,509 thousand of notes due by 2028 4.47x, so near-term default and refinancing risk is low. Second, operating leverage is working: nine-month 2026 costs rose 4.62% against revenue growth of 15.07%, which lifted free cash flow to USD 570,998 thousand. Third, all debt is unsecured and ranks equally, with no maturity in 2029, 2031 or 2032, so no creditor class is prime and the wall is spread to 2034. Fourth, capital intensity is 2.94% of revenue, which keeps conversion of earnings to cash high and gives capex flexibility. Fifth, the platform reaches 977 million monthly and 495 million daily users, which supports advertising and subscription volumes. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 38–41; calculation C04; calculation C08; calculation C10

The five main weaknesses rank as follows. First, EBITDA before add-backs of USD 59,536 thousand is 0.91% of revenue against adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,223,341 thousand, so leverage and cover on the adjusted measure overstate capacity. Second, platform-harm litigation and regulation are unsized and insurers contest coverage, so cash claims could arrive outside debt. Third, buybacks exceeded free cash flow by USD 590,658 thousand over FY2023 to nine months 2026, so the liquidity cushion is eroding. Fourth, advertising is 80.38% of revenue with growth of 5.33% and North America daily users declining, so the core revenue line is slowing. Fifth, founder control with no note-level limits on debt or payouts leaves financial policy to discretion. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 27–30; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C02; calculation C06; calculation C11

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The sources describe no sponsor buyout, pending merger or change of control; Snap's transactions are refinancings and buybacks that it funds itself. In February 2025 it sold USD 1.50 billion of unsecured senior notes due 2033 and in August 2025 USD 550.0 million due 2034, receiving net proceeds of USD 1.47 billion and USD 541.1 million, and used them for privately negotiated repurchases of convertible notes due 2026, 2027 and 2028: USD 1,642.7 million of principal in February and USD 589.5 million in August, at USD 190.1 million and USD 37.7 million below carrying value, which produced gains of USD 66.9 million and USD 29.8 million. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C08

The exchanges moved much of the 2026 to 2028 maturities out to 2033 and 2034 but raised the cost of the debt: contractual interest on the notes was USD 109,203 thousand in nine months 2026 against USD 74,797 thousand a year earlier, and the issuer's schedule shows USD 145.3 million of interest due within twelve months. The USD 1.05 billion revolving facility was amended in February 2025 to extend USD 800.0 million to 2030 and to raise the minimum-liquidity covenant to USD 800.0 million; USD 250.0 million of it still expires in May 2027, and the convertible notes due 2026 were repaid at maturity in August 2026. In 2026 Snap bought businesses for USD 88.1 million, of which USD 68.3 million was cash, paid partly in Class A shares, and on 4 November 2026 its equity-plan share reserve was enlarged, adding about 2.61% to the share count if fully issued. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-03-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 156; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 164; calculation C09; calculation C15

fields.value: Snap Inc (issuer id snap-1564408), as of 2026-11-18, pathway credit snapshot. Scope: statement tables, debt and liquidity data and credit ratios from the five supplied SEC filings, in the issuer's own currency. The Source readiness output of this run is the only earlier input.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Snap's leverage is 2.85x on issuer-adjusted EBITDA but not meaningful on reported EBITDA, which treats stock-based compensation as a cost, so the credit case rests on cash generation and liquid assets rather than earnings cover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For the last twelve months to 30 September 2026, total debt is 58.56x reported EBITDA and 2.85x adjusted EBITDA, and cash interest paid is covered 0.39x and 8.10x respectively. On adjusted EBITDA, leverage has fallen from 23.21x in FY2023 as the issuer's own measure grew and carrying debt declined. Reported EBITDA was negative in every fiscal year to FY2025, so those ratios are not calculable. Net debt counts cash and cash equivalents only: it is 41.44x reported and 2.02x adjusted EBITDA, and the investment portfolio is not netted.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 55–56; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 144; calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation C07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has fallen sharply on the issuer's own EBITDA, but its level depends on an add-back that is a recurring cost. Total debt at carrying value over issuer-adjusted EBITDA fell from 23.21x for FY2023 to 7.16x for FY2024, 5.13x for FY2025 and 2.85x for the last twelve months to 30 September 2026, because adjusted EBITDA grew from USD 161.577 million to USD 1,223.341 million while carrying debt declined from USD 3,749.400 million to USD 3,486.418 million. The adjusted measure adds back about USD 1.0 billion a year of stock-based compensation, so reported EBITDA, which treats it as a cost, was negative in each fiscal year to FY2025 and is USD 59.536 million for the last twelve months. Creditors gain from the improvement on both measures, but a leverage level that depends on excluding a compensation cost paid in equity is only as reliable as the equity currency that pays it.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest cover is adequate on the adjusted measure and thin on the reported one, and the coupon step-up is recent. Cash interest paid rose from USD 10.244 million in FY2023 to USD 65.060 million in FY2025 and about USD 151.060 million for the last twelve months, because the 2033 and 2034 senior notes (USD 2,050.000 million of principal issued in 2025) replaced low-coupon convertible notes; the issuer states future interest obligations of USD 145.3 million within a year and USD 824.5 million thereafter. Cover is 8.10x on adjusted EBITDA but 0.39x on reported EBITDA, so every dollar of cash coupon is serviced from cash flow that includes a large non-cash compensation add-back rather than from earnings after that cost.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flow is the strongest support but is flattered by stock-based compensation, and shareholder returns absorb all of it. Free cash flow was USD 776.554 million for the last twelve months, 63.48% of adjusted EBITDA and 11.83% of revenue, with capital intensity of only 3.14% of revenue because the platform runs on third-party hosting and leased offices. Operating cash flow includes the non-cash compensation add-back of USD 1,016.825 million in FY2025, so the figure is not comparable with a business that pays staff in cash; and share repurchases of USD 600.964 million in nine months 2026 exceeded nine-month free cash flow of USD 570.998 million, so the excess came out of cash and the securities portfolio.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is large against near-term maturities, and the facility covenant is tested on cash and cash equivalents rather than on the whole portfolio. Cash and cash equivalents of USD 1,019.215 million, marketable securities of USD 1,751.432 million and an undrawn USD 1,050.000 million revolving facility compare with USD 106.318 million of 2027 convertible notes due on 1 May 2027 and a USD 250.000 million facility tranche expiring on 6 May 2027. Net debt on cash and cash equivalents alone is USD 2,467.203 million, or USD 715.771 million if marketable securities are netted. The facility's minimum-liquidity covenant of USD 800.000 million is defined on unrestricted cash and cash equivalents, a line that excludes marketable securities on the balance sheet; whether the agreement counts the securities is not stated, and this module computes no covenant headroom.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The one non-debt funding float is deferred revenue, which is growing and is not debt. Deferred revenue inside accrued expenses rose from USD 145.2 million at 31 December 2025 to USD 246.6 million at 30 September 2026 alongside growth in other revenue, mainly subscriptions; it is a prepayment for service delivered, carries no interest and is outside net debt. No supplier finance, factoring or customer-deposit arrangement is described in any source.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No event after the 30 September 2026 balance sheet changes net debt, and the multi-figure debt items are kept apart by purpose. The share-reserve increase approved on 4 November 2026 does not touch net debt, and the February 2026 repurchase programme of USD 500.0 million, of which USD 150.0 million remained at 30 September 2026, is a discretionary outflow after FY2025 and is excluded from period figures. The 2025 note exchanges leave two debt figures: principal of USD 3,420.509 million, used for the maturity ladder, and carrying value of USD 3,486.418 million, used for leverage, which includes a USD 106.943 million premium on the 2033 notes created by debt-modification accounting.

fields.value: Three data limits restrict the ratios and two definition differences matter. Reported EBITDA is calculated because the issuer reports only an adjusted figure; interim cash interest is stated to one decimal in USD millions, so last-twelve-months cover is an estimate; and the fourth quarter of 2025 is constructed because no fourth-quarter statements are supplied. The issuer's reconciliation also uses depreciation and compensation figures that differ from the cash flow statement by restructuring-related amounts (USD 1.374 million and USD 26.071 million for nine months 2026), and its cash interest paid is lumpy because the senior notes pay semi-annually, so a quarter's cash interest is not a run rate.

Severity Medium. The action is to supply the indentures and the credit agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Snap Inc (issuer id snap-1564408), as of 2026-11-18, pathway credit snapshot. Scope: business, ownership and control, governance, capital-return behaviour and issuer history from the five supplied SEC filings, read with the Source readiness output of this run.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Snap's creditors depend on founder discretion rather than contract: the two co-founders hold over 99% of the votes, the notes carry no stated limit on debt, liens, buybacks or dividends, and conduct so far has been creditor-neutral to supportive.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The founders own 19.59% of the shares, so the votes and the economics are far apart, and buybacks of USD 600,964 thousand in nine months 2026 exceeded free cash flow of USD 570,998 thousand. Advertising fell to 80.38% of nine-month revenue from 87.82% as other revenue grew 85.31%, but the filings do not show how much of that growth recurs. Litigation losses cannot be estimated and insurers dispute coverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 39–40; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 246–250; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 156; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 27–30; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C05; calculation C07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control sits with two people and does not depend on how much equity they own. Mr Spiegel and Mr Murphy hold 53.13% and 46.40% of the votes through ten-vote Class C shares, 99.54% together, while the non-voting Class A shares that make up most of the equity carry no say. Their combined economic interest was 19.59% at the end of 2025, down from 20.68% a year earlier as their Class A holdings fell with no loss of votes, and any future Class A stock dividend would prolong that control. Any merger or sale of the company needs only their consent, and the notes' only reaction to one is a put on a change of control, at 101% of principal for the senior notes and 100% for the convertible notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 39–40; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 247; 10-K_2024-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 202; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 77–78; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 22; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation C06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The board is independent in form but is not a counterweight to the founders. Ten of twelve directors at the end of 2025 were non-employee directors the board judged independent, the chair is independent, Snap has not used the controlled-company exemption, and the audit, compensation and nominating committees are each made up of independent directors. Yet the 2026 directors were elected by written consent of the Class C holders, so no outside vote can remove them, and the thirteenth name elected that day does not appear in the annual report's director list and is not stated to be independent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 209–213; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 256; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-06-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 160; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The notes give creditors almost no contractual protection against a change in financial policy; only the revolving facility does. The annual report and each later quarterly report say the indentures do not restrict additional debt, secured debt, buybacks, investments, dividends or debt recapitalisations, while the revolving facility limits new debt, liens, intercompany transactions, dividends and buybacks and, since February 2025, requires at least USD 800.0 million of unrestricted cash and cash equivalents instead of USD 300.0 million. The size of each basket is not established because the executed indentures and credit agreement are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 156; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 143; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 26; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Behaviour to date is creditor-neutral to supportive, with one watch point. Snap has never paid a cash dividend, ran three USD 500.0 million buyback programmes without net new borrowing, and in 2025 replaced USD 2,232.2 million of convertible notes due 2026 to 2028, bought back USD 227.8 million below carrying value, with USD 2,050.0 million of unsecured senior notes that rank equally with the convertible notes that remain, giving no one security or priority. The watch point is pace: nine-month 2026 buybacks exceeded free cash flow by 5.25%, USD 150.0 million of the latest programme remains available, and contractual interest on the notes rose 46.00% to USD 109,203 thousand in the same nine months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 160; calculation C07; calculation C08; calculation C09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Related-party leakage is small and approved by independent committees, but it is concentrated in the founders' circle. Snap paid USD 52.3 million to a law firm where the chief executive's father is a partner and USD 5.5 million to one where his stepmother is a partner in 2025, together 0.97% of FY2025 revenue; it leases aircraft from entities the founders control for USD 0 while paying their running costs, and pledged USD 3.0 million to a foundation the founders set up. The annual report states that no 2025 related-person transaction fell outside the approval policy.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is shifting its mix and margin in the right direction, but advertising still funds most of it. Advertising was 80.38% of nine-month 2026 revenue against 87.82% a year earlier and grew only 5.33%; other revenue rose 85.31% and supplied 68.95% of the revenue increase, with the issuer attributing it to subscriptions. Gross margin rose to 59.13% from 53.33% as content and developer partner costs fell to 7.01% of revenue from 11.09%. The other-revenue line also holds a fixed-fee partner contract with USD 387.9 million of unsatisfied obligations at the end of 2025 running only into the first quarter of 2027, and the filings do not split subscriptions from that contract.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 36–37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 171–172; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C11; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: North America is the weak spot in a platform that depends on three outside providers. Daily active users grew 4% in the third quarter of 2026, but the growth rate printed for North America was a decline of 6% and for Europe a decline of 1%, against 9% growth in Rest of World, while North America still produced 55.84% of nine-month revenue. Snap runs most of its computing on Google Cloud and AWS, relies on Google, Apple and Amazon for operating systems and services, and carries USD 2.6 billion of non-cancelable commitments largely due within three years; from the first quarter of 2027 it will stop reporting regional daily users and regional revenue per user, which removes the clearest view of that weakness.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 38–41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 74–75; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C03

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Litigation and regulation are the one claim on cash that the filings cannot size. Thousands of plaintiffs allege that the platform harms minors, state attorneys general trials start in August 2027, the European Commission opened a Digital Services Act proceeding on 26 March 2026, and insurers contest coverage with a hearing set for 10 December 2026; Snap says no loss can be estimated; the first four bellwether trials were settled confidentially, a school-district case also settled, and settlements to date had no material effect. Snap's own risk factor cites a competitor settlement of over USD 12 billion and states that its resources are substantially more limited.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management continuity is intact at the top but unexplained in finance. The Chief Financial Officer named in the quarterly report signed on 6 May 2026 was Mr Andersen, the reports signed on 3 August and 4 November 2026 name Mr Hott, and the sources give no reason; a general counsel joined in November 2025 and the April 2026 plan to cut about 16% of staff cost USD 128,505 thousand in nine months, inside the issuer's estimated range of USD 95 million to USD 130 million. The founders' contractual salary is USD 1, and their employment terms renew automatically for five years from 1 January 2027 unless ended.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 158; 10-Q_2026-06-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 162; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 165; 10-Q_2026-03-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 227–228; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 251; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is the record. No cash dividend has ever been declared, buybacks have come from cash rather than new debt, the revolving facility's liquidity covenant was raised to USD 800.0 million in 2025, the 2025 refinancing was unsecured and ranks equally with the notes it replaced, internal control over financial reporting was effective at the end of 2025, and cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of USD 2.8 billion are large against the USD 150.0 million left on the buyback programme. Revenue grew 15.07% in nine months 2026, and the founders' disclosed holdings are Snap shares, which a credit failure would impair.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would turn more negative on a debt-funded buyback or distribution, any secured or priming debt, a non-pro-rata exchange, repurchases that keep exceeding free cash flow while cash and cash equivalents of USD 1,019,215 thousand move toward the facility's USD 800.0 million floor, or a litigation outcome that is large against cash and uninsured. It would turn more positive if the executed documents show tight baskets on restricted payments and liens, if subscription revenue is shown with subscriber counts and holds after the partner contract ends, and if the insurance dispute is resolved in Snap's favour.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 49–51; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 200; calculation C02; calculation C07; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed indentures, the credit agreement and the list of subsidiaries are not supplied, so the finding that contract protection is thin rests on the issuer's own risk-factor wording and could be too negative if the documents hold baskets or definitions that wording omits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ownership is dated 31 December 2025 and the Tencent line is the issuer's estimate from a 2021 report by Tencent, so the founders' economic interest of 19.59% may be overstated after their 2026 trading plans, which would weaken the alignment argument but not the control finding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The reason for the change in Chief Financial Officer and the role of an executive hired under a September 2026 agreement are not stated, so the continuity finding cannot tell planned succession from stress.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Subscription and partner revenue are not reported separately and no subscriber count is stated, so the diversification finding cannot say how much of the 85.31% growth in other revenue recurs once the partner contract ends.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Regional user and revenue-per-user values appear only as charts whose growth-rate text was extracted, with the two developed-region series told apart by heading order and checked against one overlapping quarter, so the North America weakness rests on growth rates, not on user counts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No accrual, loss range or insurance recovery is stated for the platform and regulatory cases, so the finding that litigation is the unsized claim cannot be turned into a cash-at-risk figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The sources describe no sponsor buyout, pending merger or change of control; Snap's transactions are refinancings and buybacks that it funds itself. In February 2025 it sold USD 1.50 billion of unsecured senior notes due 2033 and in August 2025 USD 550.0 million due 2034, receiving net proceeds of USD 1.47 billion and USD 541.1 million, and used them for privately negotiated repurchases of convertible notes due 2026, 2027 and 2028: USD 1,642.7 million of principal in February and USD 589.5 million in August, at USD 190.1 million and USD 37.7 million below carrying value, which produced gains of USD 66.9 million and USD 29.8 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The exchanges moved much of the 2026 to 2028 maturities out to 2033 and 2034 but raised the cost of the debt: contractual interest on the notes was USD 109,203 thousand in nine months 2026 against USD 74,797 thousand a year earlier, and the issuer's schedule shows USD 145.3 million of interest due within twelve months. The USD 1.05 billion revolving facility was amended in February 2025 to extend USD 800.0 million to 2030 and to raise the minimum-liquidity covenant to USD 800.0 million; USD 250.0 million of it still expires in May 2027, and the convertible notes due 2026 were repaid at maturity in August 2026. In 2026 Snap bought businesses for USD 88.1 million, of which USD 68.3 million was cash, paid partly in Class A shares, and on 4 November 2026 its equity-plan share reserve was enlarged, adding about 2.61% to the share count if fully issued.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-03-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 156; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 164; calculation C09; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The risk level is driven by founder control that no outside party can check and by notes that carry no stated restriction on debt or payouts, because the founders can change financial policy without creditor consent, which implies exposure to a debt-funded payout or priming that the sources do not show has happened. Countervailing evidence is a clean record of cash-funded buybacks, no dividends, a tighter liquidity covenant, independent committees and USD 2.8 billion of cash and securities. Further analysis requires the executed indentures and credit agreement, the guarantor list and loss estimates for the platform cases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance review completed with limitations. Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. Key gaps: executed legal documents, litigation loss estimates, reasons for the finance leadership change and current founder holdings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Snap Inc (issuer id snap-1564408), as of 2026-11-18, pathway credit snapshot. Scope: fundamental credit synthesis from the five supplied SEC filings, read with the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance outputs of this run.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Snap presents an adequate, improving fundamental credit anchored by liquidity rather than earnings: USD 2.8 billion of cash and securities covers debt due before 2030 more than four times, while earnings before stock-compensation add-backs are near zero and litigation is unsized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage of 2.85x on issuer-adjusted EBITDA hides that this measure excludes USD 1,025,256 thousand a year of stock-based compensation, which Snap offsets with buybacks that exceeded free cash flow in every year since 2023; liquid assets fell 17.94% from the end of 2024. The first maturities are modest, USD 106,318 thousand of convertible notes and a USD 250.0 million facility tranche in May 2027, so the credit is more exposed to slow erosion of liquidity and to the platform-harm cases than to a refinancing squeeze.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 49; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C03; calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is the anchor of the credit and is large against what falls due, but it is being spent. Cash and cash equivalents of USD 1,019,215 thousand plus marketable securities of USD 1,751,432 thousand give liquid assets of USD 2,770,647 thousand, which is 4.47x the USD 620,509 thousand of notes due by 2028 and 0.81x all principal of USD 3,420,509 thousand, before an undrawn USD 1.05 billion revolving facility. Liquid assets nonetheless fell by USD 605,632 thousand, or 17.94%, from the end of 2024, a period in which buybacks exceeded free cash flow by USD 590,658 thousand, and the cushion will keep shrinking if buybacks continue to run above free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 155–156; calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings quality is the main constraint: EBITDA before add-backs is close to zero and the issuer's adjusted measure leaves out a recurring cost that Snap pays for in cash through buybacks. For the last twelve months to 30 September 2026, EBITDA before add-backs was USD 59,536 thousand, 0.91% of revenue, against issuer-adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,223,341 thousand, and stock-based compensation of USD 1,025,256 thousand is most of the gap. In nine months 2026 the shares Snap repurchased equalled 100.62% of the shares that vested from stock awards, so buybacks of USD 600,964 thousand did little more than hold the Class A share count, which rose 0.41%. Free cash flow of USD 776,554 thousand therefore overstates what is left for creditors, and counting stock pay as a cash cost would make it negative USD 248,702 thousand, an analyst normalisation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 144; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 56; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C05; calculation C09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is moderate on the issuer's measure and unreadable on the unadjusted one, so debt service has to be judged on cash. Total debt at carrying value of USD 3,486,418 thousand at 30 September 2026 is 2.85x last twelve months issuer-adjusted EBITDA but 58.56x last twelve months EBITDA before add-backs, and cash interest paid of USD 151.06 million over the same period is covered 8.10x and 0.39x respectively. Free cash flow covers the USD 145.3 million of interest due within a year 5.34x, so debt service is comfortable on cash, but the interest bill is stepping up as the 2025 refinancing replaced near-zero-coupon convertible notes with senior notes, with contractual interest on the notes up 46.00% in nine months 2026. Net of both cash lines, debt is USD 715,771 thousand.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 155; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Maturities are well spaced, and the refinancing test comes in 2028, not 2027. Only USD 106,318 thousand of convertible notes due on 1 May 2027 and an undrawn USD 250.0 million facility tranche expiring on 6 May 2027 fall due before 2028, and the USD 514,191 thousand of convertible notes due in March 2028 is the first large maturity. The convertible notes cannot be counted on to convert: the April 2026 average buyback price of USD 5.15 was 23.22% of the 2030 notes' conversion price of USD 22.18 and the if-converted value stayed below principal, so they behave as cash debt. The 2033 and 2034 senior notes were quoted at 94.56% and 93.85% of principal at 30 September 2026, about 9 points lower than at the end of 2025, so market access exists but is priced; replacing the 2028 and 2030 convertible notes at the senior notes' rate would add USD 82.52 million a year of interest, 10.63% of last twelve months free cash flow, on the analyst's assumption.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 19–24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-03-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 156; 10-Q_2026-06-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 160; calculation C08; calculation C13; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue durability is average at best: revenue is growing, but advertising is short-cycle, concentrated and slowing. Advertising is 80.38% of nine-month 2026 revenue and grew 5.33% against 15.07% for total revenue; most advertisers have no long-term commitments, and Snap states that demand growth on its advertising platform has slowed and that platform policy changes have hurt targeting and measurement, particularly in North America, where the growth in daily users was negative 6% in the third quarter of 2026. Other revenue, up 85.31%, includes a fixed-fee partner contract with USD 387.9 million unsatisfied at the end of 2025 that is disclosed only through the first quarter of 2027, and the part that is subscriptions is not reported.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 38–41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 172; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margin resilience is improving because costs are almost flat, which is real but partly one-off. In nine months 2026 revenue rose 15.07% while total costs rose 4.62%, an incremental operating margin of 65.08%, and in the third quarter revenue rose 14.31% against a 0.65% rise in costs, turning an operating loss of USD 128,362 thousand into an operating profit of USD 76,716 thousand. Gross margin rose to 59.13% from 53.33% as content and developer partner costs fell, and the 16% headcount reduction cost USD 128,505 thousand, inside the issuer's estimate of USD 95 million to USD 130 million. The savings rely on cuts that cannot repeat, hosting and other commitments of USD 1,609,584 thousand in 2026 and USD 1,075,237 thousand in 2027 floor the cost base, and the same operating leverage works in reverse if revenue stalls.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 44–46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; 10-Q_2026-03-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 186; calculation C10; calculation C12; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is a genuine strength, but the cash goes to equity holders first. Purchases of property and equipment are only 2.94% of revenue because hosting is rented, so last twelve months free cash flow is 63.48% of issuer-adjusted EBITDA and 11.83% of revenue, and nine-month 2026 free cash flow of USD 570,998 thousand is more than double the USD 231,633 thousand of a year earlier. Buybacks took USD 600,964 thousand of it and more, and fourth-quarter seasonality adds support, since fourth-quarter 2025 revenue was 13.91% above the third quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 143; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 155; calculation C04; calculation C06; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Platform-harm litigation and regulation are the primary downside path and cannot be sized. Thousands of plaintiffs allege that the platform harms minors, attorney general trials are set for August 2027, the European Commission opened proceedings under the Digital Services Act on 26 March 2026, and insurers contest coverage, with a hearing on 10 December 2026. Snap states that no loss can be estimated, settlements so far were not material and a USD 65.0 million securities settlement was covered by insurance, but the filing cites a competitor settlement of over USD 12 billion, a reminder that these claims sit outside debt and outside the figures above. Liquid assets are large against anything disclosed, so the effect would arrive first as lost cushion rather than as a payment default.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 27–30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 131–132; 10-Q_2026-06-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 25; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the swing factor: founder control, thin note-level limits and a buyback habit mean creditors rely on restraint. The Business & governance review found two founders with over 99% of the votes, indentures that do not restrict debt, liens or payouts, and a revolving facility whose USD 800.0 million minimum-liquidity covenant tests cash and cash equivalents, which were USD 1,019,215 thousand at 30 September 2026; headroom is not computed because the covenant is known only from a summary. Nothing documented is creditor-adverse, but nothing in the notes prevents it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is the speed of improvement. Third-quarter 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of USD 382,647 thousand was 110.20% above the prior-year quarter, the quarter produced net income of USD 56,498 thousand against a loss of USD 103,541 thousand, nine-month free cash flow more than doubled, no debt is secured, no maturity falls in 2029, 2031 or 2032, and the issuer says existing cash is enough for at least twelve months. Buybacks are discretionary and can be stopped at once, which would turn the liquidity trend around without any change in operations, and the 2030 convertible notes' conversion price makes equity dilution from the debt very unlikely.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would weaken on advertising revenue turning negative year on year, North America daily-user declines spreading, a ruling for the insurers on 10 December 2026, a sizeable verdict or settlement in the 2027 trials, buybacks continuing above free cash flow while cash and cash equivalents approach the USD 800.0 million covenant floor, or any debt-funded payout or secured debt. It would strengthen if EBITDA before add-backs stays above cash interest through the seasonally weak quarters, if stock-based compensation falls as a share of revenue, if subscription revenue is shown to be recurring, and if the executed documents show tight limits on payouts and liens.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C06; calculation C08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer set, agency rating or market price series is supplied, so the judgement that the profile is adequate is absolute rather than relative to comparable high-yield issuers and could shift when benchmarked.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The covenant definition and any other maintenance test are known only from a summary, and the sources do not say whether standby letters of credit reduce the revolving facility's availability, so the liquidity finding counts the facility at its face amount and no covenant headroom is computed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Loss estimates, accruals and insurance recoveries for the platform-harm and regulatory cases are not stated, so the downside path is qualitative and the cash that could leave outside debt cannot be bounded.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The split of other revenue between subscriptions and the partner contract is not reported, so the revenue durability finding cannot judge how much of the 85.31% growth continues after the first quarter of 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The fourth quarter of 2025 is derived from the annual report and nine-month comparatives, and interim cash interest is given to one decimal, so the last twelve months cover and seasonality figures carry rounding error of roughly USD 0.1 million on interest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The outlook rests on trend because the issuer provides only limited financial guidance, so the improving direction in the view may not hold if the fourth-quarter advertising season disappoints.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The five main strengths rank as follows. First, liquid assets of USD 2,770,647 thousand cover the USD 620,509 thousand of notes due by 2028 4.47x, so near-term default and refinancing risk is low. Second, operating leverage is working: nine-month 2026 costs rose 4.62% against revenue growth of 15.07%, which lifted free cash flow to USD 570,998 thousand. Third, all debt is unsecured and ranks equally, with no maturity in 2029, 2031 or 2032, so no creditor class is prime and the wall is spread to 2034. Fourth, capital intensity is 2.94% of revenue, which keeps conversion of earnings to cash high and gives capex flexibility. Fifth, the platform reaches 977 million monthly and 495 million daily users, which supports advertising and subscription volumes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 38–41; calculation C04; calculation C08; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The five main weaknesses rank as follows. First, EBITDA before add-backs of USD 59,536 thousand is 0.91% of revenue against adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,223,341 thousand, so leverage and cover on the adjusted measure overstate capacity. Second, platform-harm litigation and regulation are unsized and insurers contest coverage, so cash claims could arrive outside debt. Third, buybacks exceeded free cash flow by USD 590,658 thousand over FY2023 to nine months 2026, so the liquidity cushion is eroding. Fourth, advertising is 80.38% of revenue with growth of 5.33% and North America daily users declining, so the core revenue line is slowing. Fifth, founder control with no note-level limits on debt or payouts leaves financial policy to discretion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 27–30; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C02; calculation C06; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Snap runs Snapchat, a camera-first messaging application used by 977 million people a month and 495 million a day in the third quarter of 2026, and monetises it mainly through advertising with a growing subscription and partnership line; it reports one operating segment, employed 5,261 people at the end of 2025 and in April 2026 announced a plan to cut about 16% of staff. Revenue is recognised as advertisements are served or ratably over periods of under 30 days for fixed-fee advertising, ratably over a year or less for subscriptions and ratably over longer terms for partnerships, so visibility is short: unsatisfied performance obligations at the end of 2025 were only USD 387.9 million, all from one partner agreement, and deferred revenue was USD 246.6 million at 30 September 2026 against USD 145.2 million at the end of 2025. For creditors the model gives fast revenue recognition and weak contractual visibility, which supports cash generation in good markets but offers little protection if advertisers cut budgets, and the history includes a 2023 AR Enterprise wind-down, a 2024 restructuring and the 2026 headcount cut, so cost resets are a recurring lever.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 38–41; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 171–172; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 144; 10-Q_2026-03-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 31; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Snap is a listed company controlled by its two founders, who hold over 99% of the votes through Class C shares and about 19.59% of the shares; the Class A shares that carry the public equity are non-voting. The consolidated group is Snap Inc. and wholly owned subsidiaries, with a United Kingdom base holding USD 256,209 thousand of long-lived assets and about 11% of cash and securities held by foreign subsidiaries; no restricted or unrestricted group, finance subsidiary or guarantor is described, so the structural position of the unsecured notes against subsidiary liabilities is not established. Creditors face leverage tolerance that is set by the founders alone, a revolving facility that limits debt, liens, dividends and buybacks, and indentures that do not, which leaves financial policy to discretion; the Business & governance review rated governance risk medium because behaviour so far has been creditor-neutral to supportive.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 143

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue growth in nine months 2026 was 15.07%, made of advertising up 5.33% and other revenue up 85.31%. Volume grew 4% in monthly and daily users and price or mix improved, with revenue per daily user of USD 3.48 against USD 3.16, up 10.13%, driven by native ad surfaces such as Sponsored Snaps and Promoted Places and by subscriptions. Revenue is discretionary, short-cycle and exposed to platform policy: advertisers spend on impression-based and short fixed-fee contracts with no long-term commitments, the issuer cites Apple's tracking changes, competition for advertising budgets and its own 2025 ad platform change, and substitution risk is high because the product is free and users and advertisers can move. There is no pass-through, customer concentration is not disclosed, and subscription retention is not reported. The conclusion is that revenue is not structurally declining but is cyclical, discretionary and partly dependent on a fixed-fee partner contract with limited remaining life, so durability supports cash flow in the next 12 to 24 months more than over the 2030 to 2034 maturities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 66–71; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 172; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The cost base is mostly people and hosting. Personnel-heavy operating expenses and stock-based compensation make up the largest part, research and development alone was 30.89% of nine-month 2026 revenue, infrastructure costs for Google Cloud and AWS were 25.07% and scale with users, while content and developer partner payments fell to 7.01% of revenue from 11.09% as advertising shifted to native surfaces and advertising partner and transaction costs rose to 8.43% with subscriptions. Operating leverage is high both ways: costs were nearly flat while revenue grew, but non-cancelable commitments of USD 3,423,854 thousand at the end of 2025, 78.42% of them due in 2026 and 2027, and a payroll partly paid in stock granted at an average value of USD 5.53 in 2026 make short-run flexibility smaller than the headcount cut suggests. Margins can be defended under moderate volume pressure through further cuts, marketing and hiring restraint, but not through the hosting commitments or the stock award pipeline, and a revenue decline would hit operating income at roughly the incremental rate of 65.08%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 36–37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 44–46; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 186; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C10; calculation C12; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital expenditure is light because hosting is outsourced: purchases of property and equipment were 2.94% of nine-month 2026 revenue, maintenance and growth capex are not split, and capitalised software development costs were not material. Free cash flow of USD 776,554 thousand over the last twelve months is 63.48% of issuer-adjusted EBITDA, after cash interest paid of USD 151.06 million, cash taxes of USD 26.716 million in FY2025 and operating lease payments inside operating cash flow, while restructuring cash of up to USD 100 million is a one-off drag and seasonality makes the fourth quarter strongest. EBITDA converts to free cash flow well, but the conversion rests on stock-based compensation that is not paid in cash, so how much is durable for debt service and deleveraging depends on whether buybacks must keep offsetting dilution; nine-month 2026 buybacks exceeded free cash flow by USD 29,966 thousand, which leaves nothing for deleveraging. Capex flexibility over the maturity wall is high, but the cash is committed to equity returns first.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 155; 10-Q_2026-03-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 166; calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is intense and asymmetric: Alphabet, Apple, ByteDance, Meta, Pinterest, Reddit and X compete for the same attention and advertising budgets with larger resources, and the issuer says demand growth on its platform has slowed, which caps pricing and margin durability. The threat of new entrants is moderate, because AI platforms and new social formats can divert users but the installed base of 977 million monthly users and the Lens ecosystem raise the cost of entry. Substitutes are strong, since default smartphone cameras, messaging and short-video products meet the same need for free. Buyer power is high because advertisers have no long-term commitments and can move budgets quickly, which makes revenue volatile. Supplier power is high in three places: Apple and Google control operating systems, app stores and data signals, Google Cloud and AWS host nearly all computing under non-cancelable commitments of USD 3,423,854 thousand, primarily hosting, at the end of 2025, and content partners share advertising revenue, so each can raise cost or cut reach. The net credit effect is a business that earns good margins when attention is high but has little pricing power in a downturn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulatory and social factors are material and change probability of default more than macro factors do. The platform-harm cases, state attorney general trials in 2027, the European Commission's Digital Services Act proceeding, the Federal Trade Commission consent order of December 2014 with biennial audits for 20 years and a 2025 referral that has since returned to the FTC all convert a social issue, the safety of minors, into possible fines, product changes and cash claims outside debt. Technological factors cut both ways: AI features, a third-party AI partnership and SPECS glasses offer new revenue but add hosting cost, regulatory and execution risk, and Apple and Google policy changes have already reduced targeting and measurement. Economic factors, tariffs and advertiser budgets matter through the advertising cycle, and political and regulatory restrictions on access could block products in some locations; foreign-exchange exposure is limited because the notes are in dollars and the dollar is the functional currency of most foreign subsidiaries.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 27–30; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 69–73; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 39–40; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 78; 10-K_2025-12-31_snap.htm.jsonl, page 163

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths: liquid assets of USD 2,770,647 thousand against USD 3,420,509 thousand of principal, an unsecured pari passu structure with no maturity in 2029, 2031 or 2032, operating leverage that lifted free cash flow, low capital intensity, and a reach of 977 million monthly users. Weaknesses: EBITDA before add-backs near zero, reliance on stock pay offset by buybacks, advertising at 80.38% of revenue, founder control with no note-level limits, and costs fixed by hosting commitments. Opportunities that could improve credit quality: sustained subscription growth, further cost discipline after the 16% reduction, buybacks held at or below free cash flow, and an extension of the USD 250.0 million facility tranche that expires in May 2027. Threats that could weaken it: adverse platform-harm outcomes with contested insurance, North America user decline, the run-off of the fixed-fee partner contract's disclosed obligations in 2027, rising interest cost on refinancing, and competitor or platform policy shifts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation C07; calculation C08; calculation C10; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position is average: Snap is a large consumer platform with revenue of USD 6,566,716 thousand over the last twelve months but smaller than several competitors by the issuer's own account. Competitive advantage is average, resting on camera and augmented reality products and a young audience, without switching costs. Business diversification is weak: advertising is 80.38% of revenue and North America 55.84% on a billing basis. Cost and capex flexibility is average: capex is light and headcount can be cut, but commitments and stock awards are sticky. Margin stability is average and improving, with a gross margin of 59.13%. Free cash flow stability is average because it is positive and growing but depends on stock pay and seasonality. Ability to refinance is average: senior notes trade at about 94% of principal, the 2028 and 2030 convertible notes need refinancing at higher cost, and liquid assets cover near maturities 4.47x. Liquidity is strong in size but eroding. Financial policy and governance is weak to average because control is concentrated and the notes carry no limits, offset by a clean record. The trend is improving; the missing datapoints are covenant terms, litigation loss estimates and the subscription split.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_snap.htm.jsonl, page 34; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C07; calculation C08; calculation C12; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the outlook is positive on earnings and neutral on liquidity. Tailwinds are the cost base after the headcount cut, native advertising formats, subscription growth, fourth-quarter seasonality and low capital needs; headwinds are slowing advertising growth, North America users, the run-off of the partner contract's disclosed obligations in the first quarter of 2027, the platform-harm trials and the insurance hearing, the May 2027 convertible maturity and facility expiry, and the loss of regional metrics from 2027. Over three to five years the question is refinancing: USD 514,191 thousand of convertible notes in 2028 and USD 750,000 thousand in 2030 followed by USD 2,050,000 thousand of senior notes in 2033 and 2034, against free cash flow that depends on equity-linked pay; sector headwinds include competition for advertising budgets, platform policy changes and rules on minors, and company-specific tailwinds include hardware optionality and AI features. The issuer provides only limited guidance, so the view rests on trend.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The scenario starts with an adverse ruling for insurers on the duty to defend and then a verdict or settlement in the 2027 attorney general or school-district trials that Snap must fund itself, arriving while North America advertising weakens and the fixed-fee partner contract's disclosed obligations run out in the first quarter of 2027. The first operational break is advertising revenue: with advertisers on short commitments and North America users already falling, growth of 5.33% turns to decline, and because costs are largely fixed by hosting commitments and payroll, operating income falls at about the incremental rate of 65.08%, turning EBITDA before add-backs negative again. Free cash flow would fall toward zero while buybacks, the first management lever, would stop; the next levers are further headcount cuts and slower hardware investment. Liquidity effect: with zero free cash flow, liquid assets of USD 2,770,647 thousand still cover the USD 620,509 thousand of 2027 and 2028 maturities and leave USD 2,150,138 thousand, so liquidity distress is avoided through 2028; the constraint is the USD 800.0 million minimum-liquidity covenant on cash and cash equivalents of USD 1,019,215 thousand, which may require holding more of the securities as cash and equivalents. Refinancing effect: the 2028 convertible notes would be refinanced at the senior notes' rate with notes already quoted at about 94% of principal, and leverage on the issuer-adjusted measure would rise as adjusted EBITDA falls. Observable triggers are the 10 December 2026 hearing, the August 2027 trials, advertising growth, North America daily users and the quarterly decline in cash and securities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Snap presents an adequate business profile supported by 977 million monthly users, improving operating leverage and USD 2,770,647 thousand of liquid assets, but credit quality is constrained by earnings before add-backs near zero, 80.38% advertising dependence, unsized platform-harm litigation and founder-controlled financial policy. Cash-flow durability appears adequate due to asset-light capex and free cash flow of USD 776,554 thousand over the last twelve months, tempered by the USD 1,025,256 thousand of stock pay that buybacks offset. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on maintaining the liquidity buffer, advertising growth and market pricing of the senior notes, with the 2028 and 2030 convertible notes the key tests. The primary downside path is adverse litigation outcomes with disputed insurance during an advertising slowdown. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement and indentures, litigation loss estimates, the subscription split and peer and rating benchmarks. Fundamental credit review completed. Top risk: unsized platform-harm litigation and regulation.
